lastText: File ClosedWhat the Steppe KeptContestedSoviet High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) · filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945: later than the historical May 1945, the price of choices that spent time to save men. The army that reaches Berlin has paid for the ground twice over: a war fought closer to the historical pattern of holding rigid lines regardless of the arithmetic, at the cost this campaign keeps returning to. The industrial evacuation was subordinated to front supply in 1941: easing that autumn's crisis at a cost in Urals production capacity that every later year of this campaign quietly pays for. The tank armies waited for the three fronts to close together and entered Prague on May 11, two days later than they did in the real war. The Izyum salient was given up before the Germans could close it. The armies, tanks and guns the real offensive lost in May 1942 went into the summer instead, and Case Blue met a southern front that had them. Germany's defeat was not a variable Soviet command decisions controlled, only its timing and its price.One Year LaterVictory arrived behind the historical May 1945, which means Soviet forces are still consolidating a front the historical record had a year's head start settling by this point.
